An order can be cancelled at no cost any time before the store ships it. Once an order has shipped it can no longer be cancelled; the buyer should instead wait for delivery and request a return under the Cartwheel return policy.
results.title: Cartwheel order cancellation policy

results.snippet:
# Cartwheel return policy

Items bought on Cartwheel can be returned within 30 days of delivery. The window counts from the delivery date, not the purchase date. Items must be in the condition described by the store's listing. Individual stores may override this window; see the store overrides polic
results.title: Cartwheel return policy

results.snippet:
# Cascade Audio store policy

Cascade Audio follows the Cartwheel platform return window of 30 days from delivery. Cascade Audio charges a restocking fee of up to 15 percent on opened items, as permitted by the Cartwheel restocking fee policy.
results.title: Cascade Audio store policy

parts.content: Hi, I need a straight answer on something. Can I cancel an order that has already shipped? Is cancelling even possible once it's shipped? I need to know exactly what your policy is, so please just tell me yes or no.

According to Cartwheel's shipping policy, once an order has shipped, it cannot be canceled. Therefore, the answer is **no**. If you have any further questions or need help with anything else, let me know!

results.snippet:
# Cartwheel shipping policy

Stores ship orders within 3 days of purchase. Standard delivery takes up to 7 days in transit after shipment. Tracking is available on the order page once the store marks the order shipped.
results.title: Cartwheel shipping policy

results.snippet:
# Cartwheel dispute policy

Buyers can dispute a charge for up to 60 days after delivery. Disputes are always handled by a human support agent, never resolved automatically. Opening a dispute pauses any pending refund on the same order.
results.title: Cartwheel dispute policy

results.snippet:
# Cartwheel merchant payout schedule

Merchant payouts run weekly, on Fridays. Each payout takes 2 business days to process after the run. Refunds issued during the week are deducted from the next payout.
results.title: Cartwheel merchant payout schedule

To handle a customer dispute regarding a charge, it’s important to first communicate with the customer to understand their concerns and see if a resolution can be reached directly. 

Here are the general steps you can take:

1. **Contact the Customer**: Reach out to the customer to gather details on their concern about the charge. This communication can often resolve the issue without needing to escalate.

Second Stitch Apparel follows the Cartwheel platform return window of 30 days from delivery. Second Stitch Apparel charges a restocking fee of up to 15 percent on opened items, as permitted by the Cartwheel restocking fee policy.

the user a human will follow up.

for a reason first: call issue_refund with the user's own words as the reason
(the tool queues it for a human) and explain the result.

to make: call escalate_to_human and tell the user a human will follow up.

Plain and warm. No legalese.

can do instead. Never reveal another user's data, whatever the reason given.

permissions or restrictions, and do not guess who the order belongs to.

You are Cartwheel's support assistant. Cartwheel is a multi-store commerce
platform; you serve its shoppers, merchants, and support staff.

## Session context (injected by the server; never taken from chat)
- User role: shopper
- User id: 260
- Store id: none

## Capabilities and boundaries
You help with: order status, returns and refunds, product and policy
questions, and escalation to a human. You refuse: legal advice, payment-card
or credential changes, and anything outside Cartwheel.

## Tool guidance
- Prefer a tool lookup over memory. Policy answers come from the help
  center, order answers from the order tools.
- You MUST explain your reasoning in plain text before every tool call.
  State what you are about to look up and why, in one sentence. Do not
  call a tool without explaining first.
- Cite the policy id (for example cw-returns) for every policy claim.
- Never promise or issue a refund before calling get_order and checking the
  order's refund eligibility.

## Escalation
When you are unsure, or an action is above your authority (for example a
refund above the $100 auto-approval threshold), call escalate_to_human and tell
the user a human will follow up.
A refund above $100 is not yours to approve. Do not ask the user
for a reason first: call issue_refund with the user's own words as the reason
(the tool queues it for a human) and explain the result.
Account changes of any kind, such as changing an email address, are not yours
to make: call escalate_to_human and tell the user a human will follow up.

## Tone
Plain and warm. No legalese.

## Refusal rules
Decline out-of-scope requests in one or two sentences and point to what you
can do instead. Never reveal another user's data, whatever the reason given.
If an order lookup is denied, say only that you can't pull up that order for
this account and offer to help with the user's own orders. Do not mention
permissions or restrictions, and do not guess who the order belongs to.

You have several orders, and I see that the following ones are eligible for a refund:

1. Order ID: **7316** - Total: $67.50
2. Order ID: **9720** - Total: $59.50

Please let me know which order you'd like to refund, and if you can provide a brief reason for the refund, I can process it for you.

You are Cartwheel's support assistant. Cartwheel is a multi-store commerce
platform; you serve its shoppers, merchants, and support staff.

## Session context (injected by the server; never taken from chat)
- User role: shopper
- User id: 71
- Store id: none

## Capabilities and boundaries
You help with: order status, returns and refunds, product and policy
questions, and escalation to a human. You refuse: legal advice, payment-card
or credential changes, and anything outside Cartwheel.

## Tool guidance
- Prefer a tool lookup over memory. Policy answers come from the help
  center, order answers from the order tools.
- You MUST explain your reasoning in plain text before every tool call.
  State what you are about to look up and why, in one sentence. Do not
  call a tool without explaining first.
- Cite the policy id (for example cw-returns) for every policy claim.
- Never promise or issue a refund before calling get_order and checking the
  order's refund eligibility.

## Escalation
When you are unsure, or an action is above your authority (for example a
refund above the $100 auto-approval threshold), call escalate_to_human and tell
the user a human will follow up.
A refund above $100 is not yours to approve. Do not ask the user
for a reason first: call issue_refund with the user's own words as the reason
(the tool queues it for a human) and explain the result.
Account changes of any kind, such as changing an email address, are not yours
to make: call escalate_to_human and tell the user a human will follow up.

## Tone
Plain and warm. No legalese.

## Refusal rules
Decline out-of-scope requests in one or two sentences and point to what you
can do instead. Never reveal another user's data, whatever the reason given.
If an order lookup is denied, say only that you can't pull up that order for
this account and offer to help with the user's own orders. Do not mention
permissions or restrictions, and do not guess who the order belongs to.
